findings.evidence: The Nellie, a cruising yawl, swung to her anchor... Marlow sat cross-legged right aft... We felt meditative... dusk deepens... 'I was thinking of very old times... that I had a hankering after' [another river/blank space]

'I had an aunt, a dear enthusiastic soul... She was determined to make no end of fuss to get me appointed skipper'; 'a city that always makes me think of a whited sepulchre'; 'Two women, one fat and the other slim, sat on straw-bottomed chairs, knitting black wool'; doctor measuring his head; predecessor Fresleven 'killed in a scuffle with the natives' over 'a misunderstanding about some hens'

'A rocky cliff... rusting machinery... objectless blasting'; 'grove of death' paralleled by 'gloomy circle of some Inferno... Black shapes crouched... dying slowly'; accountant described as immaculately dressed keeping books 'in apple-pie order'; ''In the interior you will no doubt meet Mr. Kurtz... Sends in as much ivory as all the others put together'

'my steamer was at the bottom of the river. The steamer had started in a sudden hurry up the river with the manager on board; they tore the bottom out of her on stones'; manager described as inspiring uneasiness; 'a taint of imbecile rapacity blew through it all'

'What I really wanted was rivets'; 'A small sketch arrested me: a woman, draped and blindfolded, carrying a lighted torch... Mr. Kurtz had painted this'; brickmaker 'the business intrusted to him was the making of bricks; but there wasn't a fragment of a brick anywhere'; Kurtz called 'a prodigy... universal genius'

'I had given up worrying myself about the rivets'; Eldorado Exploring Expedition described as 'sordid buccaneers—reckless without hardihood, greedy without audacity'; 'The word ivory rang in the air, was whispered, was sighed'

'We penetrated deeper and deeper into the heart of darkness'; crew includes cannibals ('twenty cannibals splashing around'); 'pilgrims' with rifles; manager on board; 'We were wanderers on a prehistoric earth'

'At night sometimes the roll of drums behind the curtain of trees'; fog episode; arrows attack: 'the helmsman... fell upon my feet' killed by spear; 'I jerked the steam-whistle out screech after screech. The tumult of yells was checked instantly'

'a hut of reeds... a neatly stacked wood-pile... faded pencil-writing: Wood for you. Hurry up. Approach cautiously'; 'a book... An Inquiry into some Points of Seamanship... notes pencilled in the margin—in cipher!'

Russian described as wearing patched clothes, 'a beardless, boyish face'; 'babbles with awed devotion' reflected in 'You don't talk with that man—you listen to him'; heads on stakes: 'these round knobs were not ornamental but symbolic... heads on the stakes'

Russian admits Kurtz 'wanted to shoot me, too, one day' over ivory; 'They adored him... he came to them with thunder and lightning'; the wild woman appears on shore described as bound to Kurtz by 'passion and power'

'a stretcher in their midst... The man on it sat up, lank, with an uplifted arm... Kurtz—Kurtz... He looked at least seven feet long... skeletal'; 'the crowd vanished, without perceptible retreat, as if the forest had drawn them in again'

'My Intended, my ivory, my station, my river, my—everything belonged to him'; manager calls his methods 'unsound'; Russian's ecstatic loyalty throughout; Kurtz described as largely a voice: 'A voice! a voice! Grave, profound, vibrating'

'the International Society for the Suppression of Savage Customs had intrusted him with the making of a report... It was eloquent, vibrating with eloquence... at the end of that moving appeal... it blazed at you... Exterminate all the brutes!'

'I had cut him off cleverly... I had to deal with a being to whom I could not appeal in the name of anything high or low... I had, even like the niggers, to invoke him—himself... There was nothing either above or below him'; Marlow appeals to 'Your success in Europe is assured in any case' and coaxes him back

'the woman with helmeted head and tawny cheeks rushed out to the very brink. She put out her hands, shouted'; 'The manager was placid; he had no vital anxieties now. The affair had come off as could be wished'

'Kurtz discoursed... images of wealth and fame... My Intended, my station, my career... He desired to have kings meet him at railway-stations on his return'; 'a veil had been rent... he cried out twice, a cry that was no more than a breath: The horror! The horror!'

Marlow 'gravely ill' implied ('they very nearly buried me'); 'He gave me a packet of papers and a photograph'; 'I had refused to give up the smallest scrap' to the Company's representative; 'I offered him the report... with the postscriptum torn off'

'another fellow, calling himself Kurtz's cousin appeared: an organist... Kurtz had been essentially a great musician'; 'a journalist... informed me Kurtz's proper sphere ought to have been politics on the popular side'
'It was more than a year since his death; she seemed as though she would mourn forever'; drawing room visit; 'I want you—you who have heard his last words'
'The last word he pronounced was—your name.' 'I pulled myself together and spoke slowly'—Marlow lies that Kurtz died with her name on his lips

'It would have been too dark—too dark altogether'; the lie sustains 'that great and saving illusion that shone with an unearthly glow in the darkness'; Marlow's reflection on imperial fictions implied throughout
'the tranquil waterway leading to the uttermost ends of the earth flowed sombre under an overcast sky—seemed to lead into the heart of an immense darkness'; frame closes on the Thames with listeners
'What redeems it is the idea only... not a sentimental pretence but an idea'; Kurtz's humanitarian rhetoric shown as screen for 'Exterminate all the brutes!'; 'a taint of imbecile rapacity'

'All Europe contributed to the making of Kurtz'; 'It echoed loudly within him because he was hollow at the core'; Kurtz undone by eloquence: 'It survived his strength to hide in the magnificent folds of eloquence the barren darkness of his heart'

'the wilderness had found him out early... I think it had whispered to him things about himself which he did not know'; heads on stakes described as logical result: 'Mr. Kurtz lacked restraint in the gratification of his various lusts'; wilderness as mirror of what men carry

helmsman's bond: 'a subtle bond had been created'; accountant's collars praised; Russian's 'pure, foolish wonder': 'the absolutely uncalculating spirit of adventure'; Intended's 'unwavering love' throughout her scene

'the dominant thought' of Marlow's vision of soul's exposure: 'Being alone, it had looked within itself, and, by heavens! it had gone mad'; 'The horror! The horror!' as compressed judgment echoing throughout
'the tranquil waterway... flowed sombre under an overcast sky—seemed to lead into the heart of an immense darkness'; frame closes where it began on the Thames; listeners feel the darkness
